title: The Messenger Level: Made and Erased

scenes.tts: Adrenaline stays outside a liver cell. How can enzymes inside respond? Watch the outer signal stop at the membrane while an inner signal begins moving. The answer must connect both spaces without carrying adrenaline across.
scenes.caption: Adrenaline stays outside a liver cell. How can enzymes inside respond? Watch the outer signal stop at the membrane while an inner signal begins moving. The answer must connect both spaces without carrying adrenaline across.
scenes.visual: Establish the carried 16:9 world and colour map. A thick GREY plasma membrane spans the frame; extracellular space fills the upper third and cytosol fills the lower two thirds. Adrenaline is a YELLOW labelled circle outside. cAMP is GOLD, synthesis machinery and arrows are BLUE, breakdown machinery and arrows are RED, Gs is GREEN. Mark the whole picture 'schematic' at lower right. Adrenaline drifts to a membrane receptor but never crosses. A faint question mark grows inside the cytosol while small ambient particles drift. The cell cross-section fills at least 65% of frame height.
scenes.narration: Adrenaline stays outside a liver cell. How can enzymes inside respond? Watch the outer signal stop at the membrane while an inner signal begins moving. The answer must connect both spaces without carrying adrenaline across.

scenes.visual: Over the same moving membrane world, show the title 'The Messenger Level: Made and Erased' for two seconds. Adrenaline remains outside, the receptor pulses, and cytosolic particles keep drifting.

scenes.tts: The receptor changes shape and activates G s inside. G s reaches adenylyl cyclase in the membrane. The enzyme turns A T P into cyclic AMP. The membrane holds the first step beside the inner messenger's source.
scenes.caption: The receptor changes shape and activates Gs on the inner face. Gs reaches adenylyl cyclase, also in the membrane. The enzyme now turns cytosolic ATP into cAMP. The membrane holds the first step beside the place where the inner messenger is produced.
scenes.visual: Zoom to the membrane without changing orientation. The receptor bends on 'changes shape'. A GREEN Gs block lights and slides laterally to a large BLUE adenylyl-cyclase block embedded in the GREY membrane. Label the active side 'cytosol'. Simple ATP chips enter the cyclase from below and transform into GOLD cAMP tokens. Use labelled blocks only, never molecular structures.
scenes.narration: The receptor changes shape and activates Gs on the inner face. Gs reaches adenylyl cyclase, also in the membrane. The enzyme now turns cytosolic ATP into cAMP. The membrane holds the first step beside the place where the inner messenger is produced.

scenes.tts: Cyclic AMP is the second messenger here. Its level changes inside after the first messenger binds outside. Many copies can carry one receptor input toward intracellular effectors. Unlike adrenaline, these copies never need to cross the membrane from outside.
scenes.caption: cAMP is the second messenger here. Its level changes inside after the first messenger binds outside. Many copies can carry one receptor input toward intracellular effectors. Unlike adrenaline, these copies never need to cross the membrane from outside.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full cross-section. Keep the YELLOW adrenaline circle parked outside with label 'first messenger'. GOLD cAMP tokens emerge repeatedly below the cyclase and spread through the lower frame. A large vertical GOLD gauge labelled 'cAMP level' grows at right as tokens accumulate. Several dim effector blocks deeper in the cytosol begin to glow, but do not name protein kinase A yet.
scenes.narration: cAMP is the second messenger here. Its level changes inside after the first messenger binds outside. Many copies can carry one receptor input toward intracellular effectors. Unlike adrenaline, these copies never need to cross the membrane from outside.

scenes.tts: The membrane step keeps making messenger while the receptor pathway remains active. Every gold token carries the same chemical information, so quantity becomes adjustable. More tokens raise the level. Their location and lifetime also matter.
scenes.caption: The membrane step keeps making messenger while the receptor pathway remains active. Every gold cAMP token carries the same chemical information, so quantity becomes adjustable. More tokens raise the level. Their location and lifetime also matter.
scenes.visual: Keep the full cell world. Each receptor pulse makes the BLUE cyclase release another short train of GOLD tokens. At right, transform the token count into the same rising GOLD gauge. A small position marker follows one group of tokens while a clock ring follows another, previewing location and lifetime without explaining downstream specificity. All elements remain labelled 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: The membrane step keeps making messenger while the receptor pathway remains active. Every gold cAMP token carries the same chemical information, so quantity becomes adjustable. More tokens raise the level. Their location and lifetime also matter.

scenes.tts: A source would let cyclic AMP keep accumulating. Phosphodiesterase provides removal. It opens cyclic AMP's ring and leaves A M P, erasing the message. That product cannot switch on the kinase that reads cyclic AMP.
scenes.caption: A source alone would let cAMP keep accumulating. Phosphodiesterase provides the opposing process. It opens cAMP's ring and leaves inactive 5′-AMP, erasing the message. That product cannot switch on the kinase that reads cAMP.
scenes.visual: The BLUE cyclase continues producing GOLD tokens at left. On 'keep accumulating', the GOLD gauge approaches its top and flashes an upward arrow. A large RED phosphodiesterase block then rises in the cytosol at right. GOLD cAMP tokens enter it and transform into muted RED-GREY chips labelled '5′-AMP: PKA inactive'. Do not draw a ring or bond. The gauge retreats from the top as removal begins.
scenes.narration: A source alone would let cAMP keep accumulating. Phosphodiesterase provides the opposing process. It opens cAMP's ring and leaves inactive 5′-AMP, erasing the message. That product cannot switch on the kinase that reads cAMP.

scenes.tts: When removal is proportional to the amount present, it strengthens as cyclic AMP accumulates. A higher level makes encounters with the red enzyme more frequent. The level settles when synthesis and breakdown match. This curve is computed from that first-order model.
scenes.caption: When removal is proportional to the amount present, it strengthens as cAMP accumulates. A higher level makes encounters with the red enzyme more frequent. The level settles when synthesis and breakdown match. This curve is computed from that first-order model.
scenes.visual: Transform the GOLD gauge into a large computed plot occupying most of the frame. Horizontal axis is 'time'; vertical axis is 'cAMP'. Draw C(t)=v/k+(C0−v/k)·e^(−kt) from stored computed points, starting at the gauge's current level C0 so the curve continues from the previous scene, but display only the plain label 'computed first-order curve'. A BLUE synthesis arrow of constant thickness enters the plot. A RED breakdown arrow begins thin and thickens with the rising curve. At the plateau, both arrows become equal width and a dashed line reads 'rates match'.
scenes.narration: When removal is proportional to the amount present, it strengthens as cAMP accumulates. A higher level makes encounters with the red enzyme more frequent. The level settles when synthesis and breakdown match. This curve is computed from that first-order model.

scenes.tts: Now keep the blue source unchanged and strengthen the red removal process. Nothing else in the cell changes during this comparison. Where will the cyclic AMP level settle: above its old plateau, or below it?
scenes.caption: Now keep the blue source unchanged and strengthen the red removal process. Nothing else in the cell changes during this comparison. Where will the cAMP level settle: above its old plateau, or below it?
scenes.visual: Keep the computed plot large. Freeze the original GOLD plateau as a faint dashed reference. Hold the BLUE synthesis arrow at the same width while the RED breakdown arrow visibly widens. Show the question 'New plateau: above or below?' across the top with two empty choice markers. The plotted curve has not changed yet.
scenes.narration: Now keep the blue source unchanged and strengthen the red removal process. Nothing else in the cell changes during this comparison. Where will the cAMP level settle: above its old plateau, or below it?

scenes.visual: Deliberate thinking pause. Keep 'New plateau: above or below?' visible. The BLUE source arrow flows steadily, the wider RED arrow pulses, and the old dashed plateau shimmers. Do not reveal or hint at the new curve.

scenes.tts: Below. At every cyclic AMP level, stronger phosphodiesterase removes more. A lower concentration is enough for removal to match the unchanged source, so the computed plateau falls. The balance returns, but at a different level.
scenes.caption: Below. At every cAMP level, stronger phosphodiesterase removes more. A lower concentration is enough for removal to match the unchanged source, so the computed plateau falls. The balance returns, but at a different level.
scenes.visual: Fill the 'below' choice in RED. Compute and draw a second GOLD curve using the same synthesis rate and a larger first-order breakdown constant. It approaches a lower plateau while the original remains dashed. At the new plateau, animate equal-width BLUE and RED arrows again. Label both curves 'computed'; show no spoken or on-screen numeric values.
scenes.narration: Below. At every cAMP level, stronger phosphodiesterase removes more. A lower concentration is enough for removal to match the unchanged source, so the computed plateau falls. The balance returns, but at a different level.

scenes.tts: G s raises synthesis, while G i lowers some forms of cyclase. Phosphodiesterases set removal. These controls change the messenger before any downstream target is chosen.
scenes.caption: Cells can adjust either side. Gs raises synthesis, while Gi lowers some forms of cyclase. Phosphodiesterases set removal. These controls change the messenger before any downstream target is chosen.
scenes.visual: The plot transforms back into the original membrane world. GREEN Gs pushes a BLUE synthesis slider upward. A separate muted PURPLE Gi block pulls the slider downward beside the label 'some cyclase forms'. Do not combine the two inputs or state their joint result. At the RED phosphodiesterase, removal continues. Adrenaline stays bound and the GOLD gauge holds steady; the departure and decay belong to the next scene.
scenes.narration: Cells can adjust either side. Gs raises synthesis, while Gi lowers some forms of cyclase. Phosphodiesterases set removal. These controls change the messenger before any downstream target is chosen.

scenes.tts: When adrenaline leaves, the receptor stops activating new G s. Active G s lingers until it splits its G T P, so cyclase drive fades. Synthesis falls back to its resting rate. Phosphodiesterase then returns cyclic AMP toward its resting level. Faster removal makes that return briefer.
scenes.caption: When adrenaline leaves, the receptor stops activating new Gs. Active Gs lingers until it splits its GTP, so cyclase drive fades. Synthesis falls back to its resting rate. Phosphodiesterase then returns cAMP toward its resting level. Faster removal makes that return briefer.
scenes.visual: Carry the same world forward. The YELLOW adrenaline circle floats away and the receptor stops pulsing. After a short lag, GREEN Gs fades and the BLUE synthesis arrow thins to a narrow arrow labelled 'resting synthesis'; it never disappears. GOLD tokens already present continue drifting into the RED phosphodiesterase and transform into 5′-AMP chips. The GOLD gauge descends along a computed curve, C(t)=Cb+(C0−Cb)·e^(−kt), toward a dashed line labelled 'resting level', never to zero; display only the label 'computed first-order return'. Briefly widen the RED removal arrow and show a second, steeper computed return to the same resting line, without numeric labels.
scenes.narration: When adrenaline leaves, the receptor stops activating new Gs. Active Gs lingers until it splits its GTP, so cyclase drive fades. Synthesis falls back to its resting rate. Phosphodiesterase then returns cAMP toward its resting level. Faster removal makes that return briefer.

scenes.tts: The message therefore has an adjustable height and lifetime. Its amount is not the response itself. Several possible effectors wait in the same cytosol. The next question is how a cyclic AMP reader turns that level into a specific action.
scenes.caption: The message therefore has an adjustable height and lifetime. Its amount is not the response itself. Several possible effectors wait in the same cytosol. The next question is how a cAMP reader turns that level into a specific action.
scenes.visual: Keep the same cross-section and colour map. The GOLD gauge rises to a moderate level and holds while a small clock ring slowly turns around it, representing lifetime without numbers. Then several unnamed effector blocks appear at different cytosolic locations. GOLD cAMP tokens reach them, but their outputs remain question marks. End by zooming toward one unlabelled TEAL effector for the handoff; do not name or explain protein kinase A.
scenes.narration: The message therefore has an adjustable height and lifetime. Its amount is not the response itself. Several possible effectors wait in the same cytosol. The next question is how a cAMP reader turns that level into a specific action.

scenes.visual: End card with one line only: 'cAMP levels reflect the balance of synthesis and breakdown.' Set it large and centred on the dark background. No title, logo, URL, subtitle or smaller line appears. A BLUE arrow enters a GOLD level bar from the left while a RED arrow leaves to the right; equal slow motion continues behind the line.
